8554.t: A nominal formation from ταμεῖν (tămeîn, “to cut up; to divide”), active aorist infinitive of τέμνω (témnō, “to cut; to hew”), though the exact morphological details are unclear; by surface analysis, τέμνω (témnō) + -ίας (-ĭ́ās).

8525.t: From Proto-Hellenic *skʰḗmə, from Proto-Indo-European *sǵʰ-éh₁-mn̥, formed from the zero grade of Proto-Indo-European *seǵʰ- (“to hold”), synchronically corresponding to ἔχω (ékhō, “to have”) + -μα (-ma).

8552.t: According to Beekes, probably from Proto-Indo-European *ten- (“stretch”), the same root underlying τείνω (teínō, “to stretch”), though the phonological and morphological details are rather unclear.

8560.t: Possibly related to ταρχύω (tărkhū́ō, “to bury solemnly”)

8510.t: Beekes marks the word's origin as unknown.

8517.t: σφάλλω (sphắllō, “to fall, to be cast down”) + -μα (-mă, suffix forming neuter nouns)

8563.t: Back-formation from ταὐτό (tautó, contraction of τὸ αὐτό (tò autó), neuter nominative singular), and equivalent contractions in other cases and genders.

8521.t: By surface analysis, σχίζω (skhĭ́zō) + -τός (-tós). Probably from Proto-Indo-European *skidtós, whence also Latin scissus and Proto-Slavic *čistъ.

8511.t: Generally considered to be from Proto-Indo-European *bʰey- (“bee”). Beekes rejects this in favor of a Pre-Greek origin possibly shared with ψήν (psḗn, “gall-insect”).

8579.t: From Proto-Hellenic *téukʰō, a thematicized formation from Proto-Indo-European *dʰéwgʰti, root present of *dʰewgʰ-.

8533.t: From σάττω (sáttō, “to cram, to stuff”) and the suffix -μα (-ma). Possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *twenk- (“to press, squeeze”) (Proto-Germanic *þwangiz).

8551.t: The suffix "-ινθος" proves a Pre-Greek origin. The form τερέβινθος (terébinthos) was perhaps influenced by ἐρέβινθος (erébinthos, “chickpea”).

8526.t: According to Beekes, undoubtedly of Pre-Greek origin.

8589.t: Oriental foreign word of unknown origin.

8531.t: There is no certain etymology. The word is similar to σκῦλα (skûla, “booty, spoils”), but their relation is unclear, and Beekes is hesitant to assign the word to Pre-Greek, assuming an interchange in initials of σ-/σκ-.

8592.t: Maurice connects τυλυφάντης (tuluphántēs, “cushion-cover weaver”), assuming influence of κορύνη (korúnē) or τορύνη (torúnē) to account for the vocalism. Furnée compares Luwian [script needed] (taluppi, “clump of dough”).

8518.t: According to Beekes, perhaps of Pre-Greek origin, apparently based on the pre-nasalization of the -γγ- (-ng-) as well as the lack of credible cognates in other Indo-European branches.

8535.t: From συγκαλέω (sŭnkăléō, “to call to council, convoke, convene”) + -τος (-tos). In the Byzantine sense, a semantic loan from Latin senātus.

8550.t: The fusion of two proto-Greek verbs: * The sense 'to rise' is from Proto-Hellenic *telne-, from Proto-Indo-European *tl̥-n-h₂-, a nasal-infixed present (the present tense system includes a N progressive aspect marker) from the root Proto-Indo-European…

8548.t: Borrowed from Latin tabla (“tablet, plank, table”).

8524.t: Probably from a Proto-Indo-European *skeh₂- (“to split”), and generally compared with Sanskrit छ्यति (chyati, “to split, hurt”), from the root छो (cho, “to cut off”).

8573.t: From τετρακοσιοστός (tetrăkosĭostós, “four hundred”) + -στός (-stós), a variant of -τός (-tós, ordinal suffix).
